decisions.reason: As a newly launched cardboard display in the firm's core range, it is still an inexpensive option to keep open while demand uncertainty resolves.
The pegboard-back variant extends the existing display portfolio, and after only one year there is too little evidence to justify abandoning it.
This quarter-pallet cardboard display fits closely with the firm's established capabilities, so management would likely continue testing it in the market.
Although the eighth-pallet format may address a narrower niche, the product is still too new and relatively low-cost to maintain as an option.
The wooden display pallet is somewhat less aligned with a paper-products manufacturer and therefore faces a higher exit risk, but it is still early to shut it down without clearer market feedback.
The media-focused quarter-pallet display serves a more specialized segment, yet the firm would likely keep it on the market for another year to learn more before reallocating resources.
